doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: Drummers: Baby Dodds, the Happys, Black Benny and Two Bits
summary: Billy lists the drummers: Baby Dodds, two men named Happy, Two Bits, Ray Dugas, Little Mac and Black Benny. Mary says Benny traveled only with Mac and played a full set; Allen adds details about Bunk Johnson, who worked with them once in Houston.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Then the drummers that we had from time to time was Baby Dots and a boy named Happy. Yeah, I never did know any other names.
There were two Happys, one was called Red Happy and the other Black Happy. Yeah. Happy Bolton. Benny, Benny the drummer. Black Benny.
Black Benny, yes. Black Benny, that's the real deal.
The drummer Happy was at Happy Bolton, a very short fellow. I never knew him. Yeah. The other Happy is Happy Goldston. He still plays down there.
Oh, well this Happy must be dead.
Yes, that's Red Happy.
He was a kind of red, light-skinned fellow with freckles. Bolton, yeah.
He played with Joe Oliver and Ori.
That's right. He was considered one of the best drummers in town.
Yes, yes. In time.
Then there was a fellow called Two Bits.
Oh yeah, Bunk Johnson once mentioned him. I never...do you know his name?
Nothing but Two Bits.
Well, Two Bits. That's all Bunk called him, Two Bits. Two Bits, yeah.
Two Bits, yeah. That's our brother. Brought him up north, too. Yes, yes. He married in Lynchburg, Virginia. I guess he's still there.
Did you ever know Bunk Johnson? Oh yeah, surely.
Oh yeah.
Did you ever work with him, too?
Well, he worked with us only once. He was down in Houston, Texas, and he came over and played with us.
He went over to Texas around 1914, I think, and stayed over that way. Yeah.

We got some Texas musicians, too, from there, from Houston. L.C. Tolan, and Marquiva Spreex, and who else? I don't remember. Well, then there was a drummer we had called Tootinan, he was from Mobile. And another New Orleans boy was Ray Dugas. Yes, yes, yes.
Ray Dugas, yeah.
Heard the name, I never knew. He was a real light fellow. And Little Mac, we would call him. Yes. And Black Benny. Those were drums.
But did Black Benny travel with you? I didn't know he ever went anyplace except for him.
Yes, yes, we taken him. You are. Yes, he could. Mac would be the only one he'd go away with because he knew Mr. Mac would come back home.
I didn't think he ever went anyplace.
Yes, he did.
He was afraid he couldn't get back home. Most people tell that he just played bass drum, but he played the whole drum set. Oh, yes, yes, he was good.
I rented a set of drums to carry along with me so he'd have drums to play. He had a bass drum, but he didn't have the output, you know.
